record.context_brief: Open symmetric equation x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2
record.original_question: Determine whether the Diophantine equation x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2 has infinitely many integer solutions that are not permutations of (x, y, z) = (1 - 6t^3, -6t^2, 1 + 6t^3) for integers t.

evidence.quote: The smallest open symmetric equation is either x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 1 (10) of size H = 25 or x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2 (11) of size H = 26, depending on whether you are satisfied with the description of integer solutions to (10) presented in [1, Section 4.4.1].
Equation (11) is open without any doubts, because we do not even know whether it has infinitely many integer solutions that are not permutations of (x, y, z) = (1 - 6t^3, -6t^2, 1 + 6t^3), t in Z.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Diophantine equation
   x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2,
with x, y, z ∈ ℤ. One classical infinite family of integer solutions is given by the Mahler parametrization
   (x, y, z) = (1 − 6t^3, −6t^2, 1 + 6t^3),    t ∈ ℤ,
together with all permutations of its coordinates.

Question: Does the equation x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2 admit infinitely many integer solutions (x, y, z) ∈ ℤ^3 that do not arise as a permutation of (1 − 6t^3, −6t^2, 1 + 6t^3) for some t ∈ ℤ? Equivalently, is the set of integer solutions to x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2 not contained, up to coordinate permutation, in this single one-parameter polynomial family together with finitely many sporadic solutions?
artifact.category_tag: Sums of three cubes / Diophantine equations
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 2 has infinitely many integer solutions outside the Mahler family (1 − 6t^3, −6t^2, 1 + 6t^3) is documented as open. Surveys on known polynomial families of solutions to x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = n (e.g., Rowland's compilation) and recent work on the smallest open Diophantine equations list this as unresolved: no second polynomial parametrization is known for n = 2, and it is unknown whether sporadic solutions outside this family form an infinite set.

status_evidence.title: Known families of integer solutions of x^3+y^3+z^3=n (E. Rowland)
status_evidence.snippet: Compilation of known polynomial parametric families; for n=2 only the Mahler family (1-6t^3,-6t^2,1+6t^3) is listed.
status_evidence.claim: Only one polynomial parametric family of integer solutions is currently known for n=2.

status_evidence.title: On the smallest open Diophantine equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses x^3+y^3+z^3=2 as an open symmetric equation; it is not known whether infinitely many integer solutions lie outside the Mahler parametrization.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude of integer solutions to x^3+y^3+z^3=2 outside the known parametric family is an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Sums of three cubes (A. Sutherland)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of computational and theoretical results on x^3+y^3+z^3=n; existence of infinitely many essentially different solutions remains conjectural in general.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond known parametric families, infinitude of integer solutions for individual small n such as 2 is not established.
